item.description:

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 PM HST Sat Aug 15 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Lala, located a short distance to the west of South Point, Hawaii.

Western Portion of the East Pacific:
An area of low pressure is expected to form well to the
west-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula
early next week. Environmental conditions appear conducive for
gradual development of this system, and a tropical depression could
form during the middle to latter portions of next week while it
moves generally westward across the western portion of the east
Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...50 percent.

$$
Forecaster Hagen
NNNN

item.title: Hurricane Lala Public Advisory Number 16
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Sat Aug 15 2026 
000
WTPA32 PHFO 160852
TCPCP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Lala Advisory Number  16
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM HST Sat Aug 15 2026
 
...LALA REMAINS A HURRICANE AS IT BEGINS TO PULL AWAY FROM THE
BIG ISLAND...
...DAMAGING WINDS AND HEAVY RAIN WILL PERSIST ACROSS THE BIG
ISLAND AND MAUI COUNTY OVERNIGHT AND SPREAD WESTWARD ACROSS OAHU
AND KAUAI COUNTY ON SUNDAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 PM HST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.6N 157.0W
ABOUT 65 MI...105 KM W OF KAILUA-KONA HAWAII
ABOUT 130 MI...210 KM SSE OF HONOLULU HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...75 MPH...120 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 310 DEGREES AT 15 MPH...24 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...988 MB...29.18 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* Hawaii County
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* Maui County, including the islands of Maui, Lanai, Molokai and
Kahoolawe
* Oahu
* Kauai County, including the islands of Kauai and Niihau
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area, in this case within the next 6 
to 12 hours. Preparations to protect life and property should now be
complete.
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area, in this case within 12 
to 24 hours.
 
Interests in the Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument should
monitor the progress of Lala.
 
For storm information specific to your area, including possible
inland watches and warnings, please monitor products issued by your
local National Weather Service forecast office.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM HST (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Lala was located
near latitude 19.6 North, longitude 157.0 West. Lala is moving
toward the northwest near 15 mph (24 km/h), and this general
motion is expected to continue overnight. A gradual westward turn
with an increase in forward speed is expected on Sunday, as the
core of the storm remains south of the smaller main Hawaiian Islands
and the easternmost Northwestern Hawaiian Islands through the early
part of next week.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 75 mph (120 km/h) with higher
gusts. This intensity of Lala is forecast to remain steady
for a few more hours, followed by a gradual weakening trend on 
Sunday as Lala passes south of the smaller main Hawaiian Islands. 
Some restrengthening is possible next week.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 175 miles
(280 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 988 mb (29.18 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Lala can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header HFOTCDCP2 and WMO header WTPA42 PHFO.
 
WIND: Damaging winds will persist across portions of the Big Island 
of Hawaii overnight, with the strongest winds expected in areas of 
higher terrain. Tropical storm conditions will continue to spread 
westward from Maui County to Oahu into early Sunday, then to Kauai 
County through the day Sunday. Wind speeds atop mountains and on the 
windward and leeward slopes are often up to 30 percent stronger than 
the near-surface winds indicated in this advisory, and in some 
elevated locations could be even greater.
 
RAINFALL: Lala is expected to produce additional rainfall of 4 to 8
inches across the Big Island and windward Maui, with maximum storm
total of 30 to 35 inches over the windward Big Island. Across the
remainder of the island chain total rainfall of 4 to 6 inches, with
maximum amounts of 8 inches, is expected. This rainfall will produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Lala,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_cp2.shtml?rainqpf
 
For a list of rainfall observations and wind reports associated with
Lala, see the companion storm summary at WBCSCCNS2 with the WMO
header ACUS42 KWBC or at the following link:
www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/discussions/nfdscc2.html.
 
STORM SURGE: The combination of a dangerous storm surge and the
tide will cause normally dry areas near the coast to be flooded by
rising waters moving inland from the shoreline. The water could
reach the following heights above ground somewhere in the indicated
areas if the peak surge occurs at the time of high tide...
 
Hawaii...1 to 3 ft
 
The deepest water will occur along the immediate coast, where the
surge will be accompanied by large and dangerous waves.
Surge-related flooding depends on the relative timing of the surge
and the tidal cycle, and can vary greatly over short distances. For
information specific to your area, please see products issued by
your local National Weather Service forecast office.
 
For a complete depiction of areas at risk of storm surge inundation,
please see the National Weather Service Peak Storm Surge Graphic,
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_cp2.shtml?peakSurge.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Lala will continue to build westward
across the exposed windward waters through Sunday. Swells will also
build over the exposed leeward waters as Lala passes south of the
islands. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and
rip current conditions. Please consult products from your local
weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 200 AM HST.
Next complete advisory at 500 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Gibbs/Evans

item.title: Hurricane Lala Forecast Discussion Number 16
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Sat Aug 15 2026 
000
WTPA42 PHFO 160854
TCDCP2
 
Hurricane Lala Discussion Number  16
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM HST Sat Aug 15 2026
 
Lala appears to have peaked in intensity earlier this afternoon
while passing near South Point of the Big Island. Since that time,
the hurricane has continued northwestward just offshore of the
Leeward Coast of the Big Island, while its satellite presentation
has gradually degraded. Despite the less organized appearance,
subjective Dvorak Current Intensity estimates from both HFO and JTWC
remain at 4.0/65 kt, which align with the latest objective estimates
from UW-CIMSS. Based on these estimates, the initial intensity is
held at 65 kt.
 
Lala continues to move northwestward just offshore of the Leeward
Coast of the Big Island, with an initial motion of 310/13 kt. A
gradual turn toward the west and an increase in forward speed are
expected on Sunday as the influence of the Big Island terrain
diminishes and Lala moves westward along the southern periphery of a
strong subtropical ridge. This general motion should continue
through early next week. By the middle of next week, a shortwave
trough moving across the northern Pacific is forecast to weaken the
ridge, causing Lala to slow and gradually turn toward the
west-northwest and northwest. Forecast confidence in the track,
however, begins to decrease by day 5 due to increasing cross-track
spread among the guidance. The latest NHC forecast lies close to the
Google DeepMind ensemble mean and multi-model consensus (HCCA) aids
throughout the forecast period.
 
Lala appears to have peaked in intensity earlier while passing near
South Point of the Big Island. The hurricane could maintain its
intensity for a few more hours, but weakening is expected by early
Sunday as Lala continues to pull away from the Big Island. Dry
mid-level air along with moderate vertical wind shear should
contribute to a deterioration of the convective structure and
support additional weakening. Some re-strengthening could occur
after 48 hours, and the NHC intensity forecast is close to the
previous advisory.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Damaging winds are expected to continue on the Big Island of 
Hawaii into the overnight hours, with the strongest wind gusts 
expected in areas of higher terrain. Residents are urged to stay in 
their shelter through tonight. Tropical-storm-force winds with gusts 
to near or up to hurricane strength will persist across portions of 
the smaller islands through Sunday.
 
2. Heavy rainfall, with life-threatening flooding and mudslides,
especially in areas of steep terrain, will continue tonight into
early Sunday over the Big Island and Maui. This heavy rain and flood
risk will continue to spread westward across the island chain
through Sunday.
 
3. Large and dangerous waves are expected to persist across portions
of the Hawaiian Islands through the weekend. Surf is building along
east-facing shores and will increase along exposed southern shores
as Lala passes through the region. This heavy surf may cause
localized coastal flooding and significant beach erosion.
